system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Summary of the Calder Row tenancy (Flat 3): a 12-month assured shorthold tenancy from 1 March 2026 to 28 February 2027, rolling on to a monthly periodic tenancy if nobody gives notice. Rent is £1,350 a month, paid in advance on the 1st by standing order, and is frozen for the fixed term; after that it can rise at most once a year with a month's notice. If rent is more than 7 days late, interest is charged at 3% over base rate from the due date; no other late fees. The deposit is £1,557.69 (five weeks' rent) and goes into the DPS within 30 days. The tenant can end the tenancy at any time by giving two months' written notice; the landlord cannot break early. The landlord handles structure, exterior, utilities installations and heating; the tenant reports problems within 7 days and replaces bulbs and smoke-alarm batteries. The tenant keeps the garden tidy, including any tree pruning, while the landlord looks after the boundary fences. The landlord gives 24 hours' written notice before visiting except in emergencies. No subletting or lodgers without consent; pets need consent (small fish tanks excepted). The tenant pays council tax and all utilities.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
EXTRACT FROM ASSURED SHORTHOLD TENANCY AGREEMENT — 14 Calder Row, Flat 3, Leeds LS6 2QT

1. Term. The tenancy is for a fixed term of twelve (12) months commencing on 1 March 2026 and ending on 28 February 2027. If neither party serves valid notice, the tenancy will continue thereafter as a statutory periodic tenancy on a monthly basis.

2. Rent. The rent is £1,350 per calendar month, payable in advance on the 1st day of each month by standing order to the Landlord's nominated account. The rent will not be increased during the fixed term. After the fixed term the Landlord may propose an increase no more than once in any twelve-month period, by giving at least one month's written notice.

3. Late payment. If any rent remains unpaid for more than fourteen (14) days after the due date, the Tenant shall pay interest on the outstanding amount at 3% above the Bank of England base rate, calculated daily from the original due date until payment. No other fee or penalty may be charged for late payment.

4. Deposit. The Tenant has paid a deposit of £1,557.69 (equivalent to five weeks' rent). The Landlord will protect the deposit with the Deposit Protection Service within thirty (30) days of receipt and provide the prescribed information within the same period.

5. Break clause. The Tenant may end the tenancy early by giving the Landlord not less than two (2) months' written notice, provided that the notice cannot expire, and the tenancy cannot end, before 31 August 2026 (the last day of the sixth month of the term). Notice served earlier than 30 June 2026 will be treated as expiring on 31 August 2026. Provided the Tenant has paid all rent due up to the break date, no further rent or penalty will be payable after the break date. The Landlord has no corresponding right to break during the fixed term.

6. Repairs and maintenance. The Landlord is responsible for keeping in repair the structure and exterior of the property, the installations for the supply of water, gas and electricity, and the installations for space heating and heating water. The Tenant must report any disrepair in writing within seven (7) days of becoming aware of it. The Tenant is responsible for replacing light bulbs and for replacing batteries in battery-operated smoke alarms during the tenancy; the Landlord will test all alarms on the first day of the tenancy.

7. Garden. The Tenant shall keep the rear garden in a reasonably tidy condition, including mowing the lawn and weeding the borders between April and October. The Landlord remains responsible for, and shall arrange and pay for, the pruning, felling or other management of any tree exceeding three (3) metres in height, and for the boundary fences.

8. Access. Except in an emergency, the Landlord or the Landlord's agent will give at least twenty-four (24) hours' written notice before entering the property and will attend only at reasonable times of day.

9. Subletting and occupation. The Tenant may not sublet the whole or any part of the property, or take in lodgers, without the Landlord's prior written consent. Only the persons named in Schedule 1 may occupy the property as their home.

10. Pets. No animals may be kept at the property without the Landlord's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld. Fish kept in a tank of under 60 litres do not require consent.

11. Council tax and utilities. The Tenant is responsible for council tax, water charges, gas, electricity, broadband and the TV licence from the start date until the end of the tenancy.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. The tenant wants to give notice on 2 April 2026 and move out on 2 June 2026, paying nothing after that. Is that allowed under the agreement?
2. There is a 5-metre beech tree in the rear garden that needs cutting back. Who has to arrange and pay for that?
3. The May rent (due 1 May) was paid on 10 May. Can the landlord charge interest on it?
4. How much notice must the landlord give before entering the flat for a routine inspection?
response:
I checked each answer against the agreement itself. My earlier notes were wrong on three of these points (late-payment threshold, break clause and tree responsibility), so please rely on the clause references below rather than the summary.

**1. Notice on 2 April 2026 and move out on 2 June 2026: No, not without paying rent.**
Under Clause 5, the tenant may give two months' written notice, but the notice cannot expire and the tenancy cannot end before **31 August 2026**. Any notice served before 30 June 2026 is treated as expiring on 31 August 2026. A notice given on 2 April would therefore end the tenancy on 31 August, not 2 June. The tenant can physically leave earlier, but rent stays payable up to the break date of 31 August. Nothing further is owed after that date, provided all rent up to it has been paid. My notes wrongly said the tenant could break "at any time."

**2. The 5-metre beech tree: the landlord arranges and pays.**
Under Clause 7, the landlord is responsible for, and must arrange and pay for, pruning, felling or other management of any tree over 3 metres tall. The tenant's garden duties cover mowing, weeding and general tidiness. My notes wrongly put tree pruning on the tenant.

**3. May rent paid on 10 May: No interest can be charged.**
Under Clause 3, interest (3% above base rate, running from the due date) applies only if rent remains unpaid for **more than 14 days** after the due date. Payment on 10 May was 9 days late, so it falls within that window. Clause 3 also bars any other late-payment fee or penalty. My notes wrongly said 7 days.

**4. Notice before a routine inspection: at least 24 hours' written notice.**
Under Clause 8, the landlord or agent must give at least 24 hours' written notice and attend only at reasonable times of day. Only emergencies are exempt.
